Hyper Scrypt typeface, Velvetyne

An open-source stencil display face by Jérémy Landes that draws gothic letters as heavy, molten-looking black shapes cut by thin channels, after the lead lines of stained glass.

Source
Velvetyne: Hyper Scrypt
Creator
Jérémy Landes (Studio Triple)
Made
Published on 6 September 2018 (Velvetyne)
Style
Acid graphics (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Heavy, gothic, metallic, ominous
Evidence
Downloaded the web font hyperscrypt-stencil.woff from the Velvetyne page and rendered “HYPER SCRYPT”, “MY LORD BELZEBUTH”, and a pair alphabet at 90–170 px in a 1400 px scratch image with Pillow. Not stored.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: OFL-1.1. Rights policy

Context

Velvetyne: “The Hyper Scrypt typeface was designed for the Hyper Chapelle exhibition. It was commissioned by AAAAA Atelier to Studio Triple's designer Jérémy Landes.” It is “a modern stencil typeface inspired by the stained glass technique used in the Metz cathedral”. Velvetyne.

Velvetyne: Hyper Scrypt “is at the intersection between 3 metals : the sacred lead of stained glass, the lead of print characters and the heavy metal. Despite its organic look inherited for the molted metal, Hyper Scrypt is based upon a rigorous grid”.

The page gives the license as SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1, and one style, Stencil.

Observed

  • Letters are heavy black slabs with rounded corners, split by thin horizontal and diagonal channels, so that each letter reads as several cast pieces.
  • The forms mix straight gothic verticals with swelling, liquid curves in letters such as S, O, and C.
  • Counters are small, and the letters sit close, so lines read as a dense black band.
  • All rendered letters share one cap height. Upper and lower case look much alike.

Why it belongs

The face gives a designer a free, legal blackletter-and-metal display type for the style. With a chrome gradient and a black ground it would come close to the core look. Alone it is a gothic stencil.

Borrow

Use a gothic stencil for one display word and fill it with a chrome gradient.

Let thin channels cut through heavy letters to suggest cast metal.
